conclusions: StreamBase explicitly requests kUninitialized and accepts the public default kOutOfMemory.
The selected API performs CHECK_LE(byte_length,kMaxByteLength) before allocation; that invalid native-size assertion is not an OOM outcome.
Actual BackingStore::Allocate checks the installed allocator maximum; a zero-length whole store has null data but a real native record.

The normal nonzero allocate path delegates to Heap::AllocateExternalBackingStore. Its conditional young GC, two old-space retry GCs and final all-available GC remain explicit original prerequisites; a single JS_RunGC is not asserted equivalent.
After allocation returns empty, the API calls FatalProcessOutOfMemory with literal site v8::ArrayBuffer::NewBackingStore and default kNoOOMDetails={false,nullptr}.

Node's OOMErrorHandler therefore selects Allocation failed - process out of memory, publishes permanent is_in_oom, emits no Reason line for null detail, invokes the actual optional OOMError report, flushes then ABORT.
The existing heap CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST/kHeapOOM entry is a distinct source operation and remains unchanged.
VM's TryNew native primitive is one attempt with no JS allocation/GC/pending/event; the embedding retry and terminal owner must be composed separately.
